attackLog.incidentOrCve: Check Point PHP2Shell Zero-Day / ESXi Wiper
attackLog.target: Check Point Security Gateways & VMware ESXi Hypervisors
attackLog.attackVector: Perimeter gateway exploitation leveraging PHP2Shell zero-day vulnerability to obtain root execution, followed by pivot into internal virtualization fabrics to execute data wipers across VMware ESXi datastores.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Deploy Check Point emergency hotfix Jumbo Take 126+ immediately; isolate management interfaces; restrict ESXi CLI/API to air-gapped jump hosts.

attackLog.attackVector: Improper neutralization of delimiters allowing unauthenticated remote actors to inject and execute arbitrary server-level commands via specially crafted control messages.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Upgrade UnrealIRCd instances to patched build 6.1.7+; implement egress filtering on daemon network segments.

attackLog.attackVector: Legacy 22-year-old type confusion flaw in object creation enabling authenticated database users to achieve host-level remote code execution under the privileges of the postgres service account.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Apply vendor update across PostgreSQL clusters; recompile and relink all external C-language dynamic extensions; enforce strict REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public.

attackLog.target: AMD SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Virtual Machines
attackLog.attackVector: Rogue cloud hypervisor manipulation coupled with malicious BIOS injection bypasses SEV-SNP memory encryption and attestation guarantees, reading guest enclave secrets and falsifying cryptographic attestation measurements.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Upgrade AMD microcode/AGESA firmware to patched hypervisor stepping; implement ephemeral sealed secrets with external hardware security modules (HSMs).

attackLog.attackVector: Physical supply chain interdiction by third-party reseller inserting daughterboards that read display memory and exfiltrate BIP-39 seed phrases over cellular bands directly to adversary command nodes.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Recall units procured via unauthorized distributor CryptoBilis; deploy firmware update verifying optical bus integrity; enforce direct-from-OEM procurement policies.

attackLog.attackVector: North Korean state-sponsored actors deploy real-time generative AI video/audio deepfakes during technical recruitment and executive video interviews to compromise workstations and siphon over $400M in assets.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Mandate out-of-band cryptographic proof-of-identity (FIDO2 WebAuthn challenges) during video sessions; restrict developer workstation access to operational production keys.

attackLog.target: German Defense Technology & Military Drone Fleet Infrastructure
attackLog.attackVector: Advanced state-nexus intrusion against defense manufacturing and drone teleoperation platforms causing lateral degradation of military surveillance drone ground support workflows.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Isolate telemetry networks; rotate ground control station (GCS) cryptographic certificates; implement micro-segmentation between production engineering and IT networks.

attackLog.target: Autonomous ERP & AP Invoice Processing AI Agents
attackLog.attackVector: Indirect prompt injection embedded in inbound PDF invoices overrides agentic execution flows, causing the LLM agent to modify supplier routing transit numbers and authorize wire transfers without human-in-the-loop validation.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Implement deterministic policy guardrails; enforce dual-custody approval (HITL) for bank credential mutations; sandbox tool-calling privileges to read-only schemas.

attackLog.attackVector: Targeted voice-phishing (vishing) campaigns re-engaging uncooperative breach victims, tricking employees into authorizing malicious Microsoft 365 OAuth consent applications to maintain persistent token-based mailbox exfiltration.
attackLog.immediateSolution: Enforce strict tenant-wide admin consent for OAuth applications; revoke all non-expiring refresh tokens; implement Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE).

deepDives.title: Check Point Gateway Zero-Day to Hypervisor Pivot: The PHP2Shell ESXi Wiper Campaign
deepDives.whatHappened: Nation-state and advanced cybercrime operators chained an unauthenticated remote code execution zero-day in Check Point Security Gateways (internally dubbed PHP2Shell) with a targeted VMware ESXi destructive wiping module. Once edge appliances were subverted to root level, attackers pivoted inward against management planes, terminating virtual machines and wiping VMFS datastore block tables, permanently destroying hypervisor infrastructure.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The exploit abuses input sanitization gaps within the web-based management portal parsing routine. By submitting an obfuscated multipart payload with shell metacharacters, the PHP runtime passes raw shell arguments directly to the underlying Gaia OS binary with root privileges. The adversary then drops an SSH tunnel and invokes esoteric ESXi CLI utilities via stolen management credentials, issuing asynchronous 'dd if=/dev/zero' sweeps against raw storage partitions.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [External Adversary] ──► [HTTP/S Exploit Payload] ──► [Check Point Gaia OS (Root RCE)] ──► [Internal Pivot: SSH/vSphere API] ──► [ESXi Datastore Wiper (VMFS Zeroed)]
remediation: Apply the emergency vendor hotfix (Jumbo Take release 126 or hotfix HF-026) immediately to all internet-facing Check Point appliances.
Segregate firewall and hypervisor management networks completely away from general operational subnets into out-of-band VLANs with strict ACLs.
Perform block-level integrity checks across ESXi storage arrays and preserve offsite, immutable write-once-read-many (WORM) backups.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Edge appliances remain the primary soft perimeter. Dual-plane architectural separation must exist between network inspection firewalls and underlying virtualization compute planes to prevent automated root-level cascading destruction.

deepDives.title: Subverting Enclave Trust: Mior & Skyfall Exploitation of AMD SEV-SNP Architectures
deepDives.whatHappened: Security researchers demonstrated the practical compromise of AMD SEV-SNP (Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging), exposing the theoretical limit of multi-tenant confidential cloud computing. Using two attack variants named Mior and Skyfall, untrusted infrastructure operators or malicious hypervisors can extract plaintext cryptographic keys and forge remote attestation cryptographic signatures.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: Skyfall exploits deterministic hypervisor-controlled memory page mapping to induce speculative cache side-channel leakages across encrypted VM memory boundaries. Mior goes further by co-opting the platform BIOS initialization sequence, injecting malicious nested page table entries before the AMD Secure Processor (ASP) locks down platform security registers. This permits the hypervisor to inject unverified code into the enclave while generating an attestation report that validates cleanly against the vendor root CA.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Malicious Host Hypervisor / Compromised BIOS] ──► [Faulty AGESA Page Table Registration] ──► [Bypass AMD Secure Processor (ASP)] ──► [Plaintext RAM Read / Spoofed Attestation] ──► [Cloud VM Keys Stolen]
remediation: Deploy updated AGESA firmware and AMD microcode packages provided by enterprise server OEMs to close page-aliasing vectors.
Refactor confidential computing workloads to rely on client-side enveloped data encryption with external physical HSM roots of trust rather than relying solely on host attestation.
Enforce strict cryptographic binding between attestation reports and short-lived TLS ephemeral keys inside the enclave.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Confidential computing mitigates commodity threats but cannot entirely replace zero-trust tenant architecture. When the physical substrate or hypervisor is fundamentally untrusted, firmware-level validation must be coupled with continuous hardware posture verification.

deepDives.title: Physical Supply Chain Interdiction: The Trezor Safe 5 Hardware Trojan Incident
deepDives.cve: MITRE T1195.001 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software/Hardware Dependencies
deepDives.whatHappened: Cryptocurrency security manufacturer Trezor confirmed that Safe 5 hardware wallets distributed via Southeast Asian authorized reseller CryptoBilis were subjected to physical interdiction. Attackers opened sealed retail packaging, added a custom parasitic surface-mount device (SMD) daughterboard to the display bus, and resealed the packages with counterfeit tamper-evident holographic packaging.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The added micro-implant bridges the physical interconnect between the secure microcontroller and the internal OLED display. As the user completes the device initialization sequence and writes down the BIP-39 mnemonic recovery phrase, the implant intercepts the raw frame-buffer signals, serializes the recovery seed words, and utilizes an integrated micro-eSIM modem to beacon the phrase via LTE-M/NB-IoT bands to an adversary-controlled server.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Reseller Interdiction: Micro-SMD Soldered] ──► [User Generates BIP-39 Seed] ──► [OLED Bus Snooped by Daughterboard] ──► [LTE-M Cellular Exfiltration] ──► [Attacker Drains Assets Remotely]
remediation: Issue an immediate physical recall of all Trezor devices procured via CryptoBilis during the identified compromised distribution window.
Implement mandatory optical x-ray and acoustic microscopy validation for high-assurance hardware cryptographic modules deployed within enterprise cold storage.
Deploy the vendor's emergency firmware update that conducts low-level bus resistance and timing impedance telemetry to identify foreign circuit modifications.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Tamper-evident tape is an inadequate defense against well-funded supply chain interdiction. Critical key generation appliances must have optical and electrical self-verifying silicon architectures and must only be sourced through direct, factory-audited distribution pipelines.

dailyQuestions.scenario: A financial firm recently uncovered that three newly acquired enterprise hardware security tokens had been physically modified during distribution by a third-party reseller to intercept and transmit device secrets over cellular networks. Which of the following security concepts specifically addresses this threat, and what is the MOST effective operational control to prevent recurrence?
options: A) Logic bomb attack; implement static code analysis on the firmware.
B) Supply chain interdiction; mandate direct-from-OEM procurement with cryptographically verified chain of custody.
C) Evil twin attack; enforce 802.1X wireless mutual authentication across corporate facilities.
D) Watering hole attack; deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR) software on all client workstations.
dailyQuestions.rationale: The scenario describes a classic physical supply chain interdiction attack (T1195.001), where a physical product is intercepted and tampered with before reaching the end customer. The most effective mitigation is sourcing directly from the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and establishing strict, tamper-evident cryptographic chain-of-custody protocols rather than using third-party grey-market resellers.

dailyQuestions.scenario: An enterprise architect is designing an infrastructure for multi-tenant confidential computing workloads on public cloud infrastructure. Recent research (such as Mior and Skyfall attacks on AMD SEV-SNP) reveals that malicious hypervisors and compromised platform BIOS layers can corrupt page table attestation reports and compromise enclave confidentiality. Which of the following architectural designs offers the STRONGEST defense against rogue hypervisor memory extraction and spoofed attestation?
options: A) Rely entirely on the cloud provider's out-of-the-box SEV-SNP attestation verification service over mutual TLS.
B) Implement client-side enveloped data encryption, bind attestation to ephemeral TLS session keys verified by an external enterprise-controlled HSM, and enforce strict microcode baseline validation.
C) Replace virtual machine enclaves with standard Docker containers running on single-tenant bare-metal hypervisors with host-based intrusion detection.
D) Shift the encrypted enclave storage to self-encrypting drives (SEDs) with pre-boot authentication managed by the cloud service provider's native key management service.
dailyQuestions.rationale: When relying on confidential computing in untrusted or multi-tenant clouds where hypervisors may be malicious or subverted, an organization cannot rely exclusively on host-provided attestation services. The architect must bind remote attestation cryptographically to short-lived ephemeral session keys verified externally by an enterprise-managed HSM, enforce strict CPU microcode baseline attestation, and envelop data before host ingestion.

detectionRules.title: Anomalous VMware ESXi Datastore Destruction and Wiping Activity
detectionRules.code:
title: Suspicious ESXi VMFS Datastore Destruction Command
id: 9b2d87e1-85bc-42f1-a3f2-202611140001
status: production
description: Detects suspicious invocations of disk destruction binaries (dd, parted, esxcli storage) targeting active VMFS datastores from non-standard hypervisor shell sessions.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/check-point-gateways-hacked-via-php2shell-to-deploy-vmware-esxi-wiper/
author: CYBERDEFENSE Global Intel Hub
date: 2026/11/14
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_binaries:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/dd'
      - '/sh'
      - '/esxcli'
      - '/rm'
  selection_cli:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'if=/dev/zero'
      - 'if=/dev/urandom'
      - '/vmfs/devices/disks/'
      - 'vmfs-destroy'
      - 'storage filesystem unmount'
  condition: selection_binaries and selection_cli
fields:
  - ComputerName
  - User
  - CommandLine
  - ParentCommandLine
falsepositives:
  - Authorized hypervisor decommissioning runbooks executed during scheduled change windows.
level: critical
